subject: fang blenny
title: A 2-Inch Fish Gets Swallowed, Bites From Inside, and Gets Spat Out

scenes.text: This fish gets eaten, then bites its way back out.
The fang blenny is about five centimetres long with two long fangs in its lower jaw. Groupers scoop it up like any small fish.
Inside the mouth, the blenny bites. The grouper's head starts quivering, its jaws gape open, and the blenny swims out unharmed.
In 2017, scientists collected the venom by letting the fish bite cotton swabs. It carries an opioid, a painkiller in the same family as heroin. Injected mice felt no pain at all.
Instead, their blood pressure crashed by nearly 40 percent. A predator goes dizzy and slow, too confused to give chase.
Groupers that have been bitten avoid the fish for life. The fangs came first; the venom was added later.

description:
The fang blenny is a five centimetre reef fish with two fangs in its lower jaw and a venom unlike any other: it contains an opioid peptide.
In tests the venom caused no pain in mice but dropped their blood pressure by nearly 40 percent, which likely leaves a predator disoriented; a grouper that takes a blenny into its mouth quivers, gapes and releases it, and avoids the fish afterwards (Casewell et al., Current Biology, 2017). The fangs evolved before the venom.
What is the smallest animal you know that fights back?
first_comment: Harmless fish on the same reefs copy the fang blenny's colours so predators leave them alone too. Which tiny fighter should we cover next?
